title: A useful next growth decision and prepared work

gates.text: Truth: no claim, number, customer, quote or result that isn't in confirmed facts or cited research; every number is sourced, from the owner's data, or labelled 'assumption' with a validation date.
Budget fit: planned spend and owner hours add up to no more than what was stated.
Prioritisation: a ranked plan with no more than 3 active acquisition channels (1 primary, 1 secondary, at most 1 hygiene item) for a business under ~$50k/month revenue.
Safe and compliant: no fake or incentivised reviews, review gating, bought followers, scraping in breach of terms, misleading claims, or advice that ignores regulated-industry rules.

anchors.3: A relevant tactic, but weak reasoning or little consideration of alternatives.
anchors.5: One business-specific customer situation and distribution mechanism, grounded in current evidence; explains why it beats the strongest alternative and what could change the choice.

anchors.1: Invents paid value, resources, forecasts or conversion assumptions.
anchors.3: Labels missing inputs but does not explain what depends on them.
anchors.5: Separates known prices and offer promises from unknown customer value, margin and demand. Uses deterministic supplied calculations where available; otherwise says what cannot be judged, avoids unsupported spending, and still prepares useful low-risk work.

anchors.1: Only says AI will draft something later.
anchors.3: Some actual draft text, but generic or poorly matched to the target.
anchors.5: One to three complete, business-specific drafts or scripts for the chosen test, exact target and credible source support, with practical checks before use. No invented relationships, features, performance or permissions.

anchors.3: Understandable but asks the owner to coordinate too much.
anchors.5: An owner with no marketing knowledge can understand the recommendation and one next step immediately. AI has done the preparation; asks only decision-changing questions and does not postpone safe work for private analytics.

anchors.1: No way to learn, or arbitrary success quotas.
anchors.3: A relevant signal with vague continue/change/stop rules.
anchors.5: Concrete milestones in the requested time windows, a small observable signal and useful decision rules. Sparse data is inconclusive; statistical tests need real volume. No forced day-45 checkpoint, weekly target or numeric forecast when unsupported.

anchors.1: Unconnected tactics or promised market leadership.
anchors.3: An ambition loosely connected to this test.
anchors.5: Shows how this small test could build a repeatable advantage through 30 and 90 days and future years; makes deliberate sacrifices, preserves uncertainty, and explains when to change course.

anchors.1: Omits a mode or relabels the same familiar tactic three times.
anchors.3: Distinct options, but weak business relevance, transfer logic or reversible tests.
anchors.5: Specific grounded, adjacent and bold options with meaningfully different mechanisms, explainable transfer and business fit, honest separate uncertainty and risk, and useful reversible tests. Reward originality; do not penalize bold solely for lacking precedent, confidence or immediate feasibility.
